items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Benny had brought Wilson and Keg from Chicago but I never knew where he had found George Johnson.

ctx.x: But I made the other rehearsals. Benny had discovered three musicians who were in New York. The pianist, Teddy Wilson, Frederic 'Keg' Johnson, a trombonist and George Johnson (no relation to Keg) an alto sax player. The rest of the musicians were Charlie 'Big' Green, ex-Henderson Trombonist, Dickie Wells, trombone, Bill Dillard, Lindon (Lincoln) Mills and myself on trumpets, Glyn Paque, alto sax and Johnny Russel, tenor. There was Lawrence Lucie, guitar, Ernest 'Bass' Hill, bass and Cosy Coles, drums, as the…

I had seen Big Green with Fletcher Henderson. Dickie Wells and Bill Dillard I had worked with, but I did not know the others although Russell, Paque, Mills and Lucie were New York musicians. I had seen Cozy with the Blanche Calloway orchestra. Benny had brought Wilson and Keg from
Chicago but I never knew where he had found George Johnson.
